thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P1 - High GPU queueing on dedicated pool cyansteel-prod-pool (tenant cs-374). GPUs at 96% avg across nodes, queue depth 680, 5xx spike to 6% in last 5m. Autoscale did not add nodes (policy=manual-burst-disabled). Links: https://metrics.redwood/cyansteel/pool, runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/dedicated-gpu-pressure
maya (oncall): I'm paged, looking now. Starting initial triage - checking queue + task logs.
Ravi (platform): I'm pulling pool config.
Elena (support): Customer CS Ops pinged us: they see timeouts ~ 10-12s, some requests 503. They asked for ETA.
maya (oncall): quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n pool-cs-374` shows backlog pods in Pending. GPU util check from grafana: avg GPU util 96%, mem pressure 88%.
Jordan (sre): Confirmed. Autoscaler logs show reason 'burst disabled by tenant policy' at 12:04:22 UTC. Looks like reserved capacity reached; burst was off.
Ravi (platform): Pool policy: `burst_allowed: false`, `reserved_gpus: 40`, current_gpus: 40, queued_gpu_reqs: ~18 -> need ~9 more GPUs to clear backlog.
maya (oncall): Options: 1) enable emergency burst (adds 10 preemptible GPUs) 2) throttle tenant QPS at edge 3) shift some traffic to fallback model (quantized v1.2) to reduce GPU per request 4) migrate tenant to transient shared pool (needs customer approval).
Carlos (customer-eng): I can message the customer for approval of emergency burst. If we enable burst we should also set fallback to avoid repeated spikes.
maya (oncall): I'm going to enable emergency burst now and simultaneously flip fallback to v1.2 for 30% of traffic. Will post commands.
Ravi (platform): standing by to run platform commands and monitor.
maya (oncall): Runbook step - enable burst:
```
# enable burst for tenant cs-374
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood/pools/cyansteel-prod-pool/burst" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"reason":"emergency capacity","add_gpus":10,"preemptible":true}'
```
maya (oncall): Running now.
IncidentBot: Action logged by maya (oncall): enabled burst +10 preemptible GPUs at 2026-03-15T12:07:14Z.
Ravi (platform): New nodes provisioning, kube events show new nodes joining. Monitoring GPU util.
Jordan (sre): Also applying rate limit rule at edge to cut CS tenant QPS by 20% as a precaution:
```
POST /edge/rules
{
  "tenant": "cs-374",
  "rule": "scale_qps",
  "value": "0.8"
}
```
Elena (support): Customer acknowledged emergency burst and gave 👍 to fallback routing. They report reduced 5xx after ~2m.
maya (oncall): Metrics: queue depth dropped from 680 -> 120 in 4m; 5xx down to 0.8%. Latency back to normal for most requests.
Carlos (customer-eng): Noted. I told CS Ops we will keep burst enabled for 30 minutes while we stabilize.
Jordan (sre): We should still follow up: why did autoscaler not trigger? Opening a ticket: AS-1347.
Ravi (platform): Preliminary cause: autoscaler uses utilization over 2m window; sudden sustained requests from batch job created short spike that wasn't captured by window and tenant had burst disabled. We'll adjust thresholds in beta.
maya (oncall): Handoff: I'm going to mark incident as 'mitigated' and hand off to Jordan for follow-up & postmortem. @Jordan please pick up.
Jordan (sre): Taking over for follow-up. I'll keep burst on for 30 mins then drain preemptible nodes. Creating postmortem doc and will include timeline + customer impact.
Elena (support): I'll draft incident customer update with timeline and ETA for permanent fixes.
CyanSteel Ops: Thanks Redwood team — CS noticed latency drop. Please keep us updated on root cause.
maya (oncall): Incident mitigated at 2026-03-15T12:15:09Z. will update channel when resolved. :thumbsup:
Jordan (sre): Incident resolved at 2026-03-15T12:42:06Z after draining preemptible nodes and confirming queue stable. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC. Assigned to Ravi & Jordan.
IncidentBot: Incident state -> RESOLVED. Incident ID: INC-2026-0315-0142. Severity: P1 -> mitigated -> resolved.
Carlos (customer-eng): Customer follow-up notes saved to ticket CS-9421.
maya (oncall): good job everyone. Quick action prevented a prolonged outage. We'll include a checklist to prevent tenant-burst-disabled surprises.
Jordan (sre): Action items: AS-1347 autoscaler fix, RB-212 update tenant defaults to allow burst opt-in on high-util events, postmortem doc link: https://pm.redwood/inc/INC-2026-0315-0142
Elena (support): I'll post customer summary once postmortem is ready.
IncidentBot: This thread will be archived with incident history.
